      "text": "Let\u0027s figure out why it\u0027s still not showing up. Run these checks in PowerShell to find out exactly where the break is.\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Check where Python and Pip actually are\n\nCopy and paste this line into your PowerShell and press **Enter**:\n\n```powershell\nTest-Path \"C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\pythoncore-3.14-64\\python.exe\", \"C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\pythoncore-3.14-64\\Scripts\\pip.exe\", \"C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\bin\\pip.exe\"\n```\n\n- **If the 1st is `True`, but the 2nd and 3rd are `False`:** \n  `pip` is simply not installed yet on your Python 3.14 build. Go to **Step 2**.\n- **If `pip.exe` returned `True`:** \n  It is installed, but PowerShell doesn\u0027t see your PATH changes yet. Go to **Step 3**.\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: If Pip isn\u0027t installed yet\n\nBecause you installed Python via the new Python Manager, `pip` sometimes needs to be initialized:\n\n1. Run this command to install/bootstrap pip:\n   ```powershell\n   \u0026 \"C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\pythoncore-3.14-64\\python.exe\" -m ensurepip --upgrade\n   ```\n2. Test if it responds now:\n   ```powershell\n   \u0026 \"C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\pythoncore-3.14-64\\python.exe\" -m pip --version\n   ```\n\n---\n\n### Step 3: Make it work directly as `pip` in your current terminal\n\nIf you edited the environment variables while PowerShell was already open, PowerShell **does not update its PATH** until you restart it (or reload it manually).\n\nTo reload the PATH right now in your current window, run:\n\n```powershell\n$env:Path \u003d [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable(\"Path\",\"User\") + \";\" + [System.Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable(\"Path\",\"Machine\")\n```\n\nThen check:\n```powershell\npip --version\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step 4: Turn off Windows Store Aliases (Common Windows 11 Conflict)\n\nWindows often intercepts `python` or `pip` with its built-in Microsoft Store dummy shortcuts:\n\n1. Open your Windows Start menu and search for **Manage app execution aliases**.\n2. Scroll down and toggle **OFF** any entries for:\n   - **App Installer (python.exe)**\n   - **App Installer (python3.exe)**\n3. Restart PowerShell.\n\n---\n\n**What did the command in Step 1 output (`True` / `False`)?** If you run into an error on any of these steps, share the message so we can pinpoint it.",

      "text": "This is a known bug with the Python 3.14 installer: Python came with the pip files, but **it never actually created `pip.exe` in your Scripts folder**. \n\nWhen you ran `ensurepip`, it looked and said *\"pip is already here, nothing to do!\"* and skipped generating the executable.\n\nRun this one command to force Python to actually build the `pip.exe` file:\n\n```powershell\n\u0026 \"C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\pythoncore-3.14-64\\python.exe\" -m pip install --force-reinstall pip\n```\n\n---\n\n### What to do right after:\n\n1. As soon as that command finishes downloading and creating the executables, run:\n   ```powershell\n   pip --version\n   ```\n   It will now find the newly created `pip.exe`.\n\n2. *(Permanent fix for all terminals)*: Because you are in an **Administrator** window, make sure it is saved to your entire system PATH:\n   ```powershell\n   [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable(\"Path\", [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable(\"Path\", \"Machine\") + \";C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\pythoncore-3.14-64;C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\pythoncore-3.14-64\\Scripts;C:\\Users\\Chris\\AppData\\Local\\Python\\bin\", \"Machine\")\n   ```\n\nNow `pip` and `python` will work everywhere, even if you close and reopen your terminal.",

        "text": "**Analyzing the Root Cause**\n\nI\u0027ve zeroed in on the psycopg2-binary issue; it seems pre-compiled wheels for Python 3.13/3.14 are unavailable. The `requirements.txt` file in Circleguard uses a specific, older version, which is likely part of the problem. This strongly suggests a compatibility problem with the newer Python versions.\n\n\n",

      "text": "This error happens because **Python 3.14 is too new** for the packages Circleguard depends on. \n\nSpecifically, Circleguard\u0027s `requirements.txt` is asking for `psycopg2-binary\u003d\u003d2.9.5` (released in 2022). Because pre-built Windows binaries don\u0027t exist for Python 3.14, `pip` tries to compile it from scratch, which fails because you don\u0027t have PostgreSQL development tools (`pg_config`) and C++ build compilers installed.\n\nHere is how to solve it depending on what you want to do:\n\n---\n\n### Option 1: The Easy Way (You don\u0027t need Python or Git at all)\nIf your goal is just to **use Circleguard to inspect/analyze osu! replays**, you don\u0027t need to build it from source:\n\n1. Go to the [Circleguard Releases Page](https://github.com/circleguard/circleguard/releases/latest).\n2. Download **`circleguard_win_x64.zip`**.\n3. Extract the folder anywhere on your PC.\n4. Double-click **`Circleguard.vbs`** inside the folder to launch the app directly.\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: If you are developing and *must* run it from source\nIf you are modifying the code and need to run it from GitHub:\n\n1. **Install Python 3.10 or 3.11** from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/) (make sure to check *\"Add Python to PATH\"* during install). Older libraries like `psycopg2 2.9.5` and `matplotlib 3.6.2` have pre-built wheels for 3.10/3.11 that install in seconds with zero compilation.\n2. In PowerShell, specify that version when creating a virtual environment inside your `circleguard` folder:\n   ```powershell\n   cd C:\\Users\\Chris\\Desktop\\circleguard\n   py -3.11 -m venv venv\n   .\\venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   pip install -r requirements.txt\n   python circleguard/main.py\n   ```",

It is compressed with LZMA, which is why text editors cannot read it.\n\nSince you fixed `pip`, you can use `osrparse` (which installs with zero issues on Python 3.14) to convert that replay into a clean **`.csv` or `.txt`** with exact timestamps, keypresses, and cursor coordinates.\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Install `osrparse`\nIn your PowerShell window, run:\n```powershell\npip install osrparse\n```\n*(This is pure Python, so it won\u0027t fail with the compilation error you had earlier.)*\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: Convert the `.osr` to a readable file\n\nRun this Python one-liner in PowerShell (make sure you are in the folder where your replay is saved, e.g., your Desktop):\n\n```powershell\npython -c \"\nimport glob, csv\nfrom osrparse import Replay\n\n# Find the .osr file in the current folder\nosr_file \u003d glob.glob(\u0027*.osr\u0027)[0]\nreplay \u003d Replay.from_path(osr_file)\n\noutput_name \u003d \u0027replay_data.csv\u0027\ncurrent_time \u003d 0\n\nwith open(output_name, \u0027w\u0027, newline\u003d\u0027\u0027, encoding\u003d\u0027utf-8\u0027) as f:\n    writer \u003d csv.writer(f)\n    #
